profile.reading:
SV2 is one of nine data centers CoreSite operates across Milpitas, San Jose, and Santa Clara that together make up the company's Silicon Valley campus, a group of interconnected buildings totaling more than 1.4 million square feet that CoreSite markets as a single integrated ecosystem rather than as standalone sites. The building sits at 1656 McCarthy Blvd in Milpitas and totals more than 76,000 square feet on its own, according to CoreSite's own site. CoreSite is a data center and interconnection real estate company that has operated in Silicon Valley for years and is now part of American Tower Corporation, a large publicly traded communications infrastructure company, giving SV2 the backing of one of the country's largest owners of telecommunications real estate.

CoreSite states that SV2 offers both AC and DC power options, backed by 2N UPS redundant power and diverse utility feeds, and the company backs the facility with a 100 percent uptime service level agreement, a guarantee typically reserved for buildings with mature, well-tested redundant infrastructure. Customers can deploy in full cabinets, private cages, or private suites, though CoreSite notes it does not offer partial cabinet configurations at this site. On connectivity, the company advertises access to more than 115 networks across the broader campus, a direct on-ramp to AWS, its own Open Cloud Exchange platform for multi-cloud connectivity, and participation in three peering exchanges, Any2Exchange, AMS-IX Bay Area, and SFMIX, along with blended internet service ranging from 10 megabits to 10 gigabits per second. Security and compliance certifications listed for the site include SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, supported by biometric scanners, key card access, mantrap entries, a perimeter fence, and round the clock video surveillance and remote hands staffing.

What CoreSite does not publish for SV2 specifically is the year the building was constructed, a technical or raised-floor square footage figure distinct from the overall building size, a specific IT power capacity in megawatts, or a current tenant list, information the company treats as confidential given the competitive, high-density nature of the Silicon Valley colocation market where its customers include many of the region's largest technology and networking companies.
profile.research_note: Operator states "76,000+" sqft (written as 76000, actual may be slightly higher); 2N UPS redundancy; 100% uptime SLA. No technical/raised-floor sqft, IT capacity MW, year built, or generator MW published.
profile.square_footage: 76,000+ sq ft (SV2 building; part of a 9-building, 1.4M+ sq ft Silicon Valley campus)

reading.body:
CoreSite SV2 is a 76,000-square-foot building in Milpitas that is one of nine facilities operated by CoreSite across the Silicon Valley region. The operator's published specifications do not include a megawatt capacity for SV2 itself, only that the nine-building campus totals 1.4 million square feet. Without power capacity disclosed, the facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from published data.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities, of which only 11 have published power specifications totaling 365 megawatts. CoreSite's Silicon Valley campus ranks 12th statewide by published megawatts, but this ranking reflects the combined capacity of all nine CoreSite buildings, not SV2 alone. The absence of facility-specific power figures for SV2 leaves its contribution to that ranking unknown.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI infrastructure, the lack of published power capacity is the binding constraint. CoreSite's scale across Silicon Valley suggests material infrastructure, but without disclosed megawatts for SV2 or its share of the nine-building total, the site provides no basis to estimate compute density or grid demand.
